title: Rabbi Abba bar Chiya bar Ashi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 7:2 (28b in Hyman’s citation). Hyman calls this a scribal error. He takes ב״ר to stand for “in the name of Rabbi,” noting that Rabbi Abba repeatedly reports teachings in the name of Rabbi Chiya bar Abba.

notes.text: The source’s compressed explanation of ב״ר concerns a report formula rather than a father-name. The supplied heading’s Chiya bar Ashi differs from the body’s Chiya bar Abba; this remains a source question.

The saved whole Guggenheimer Shabbat 7:2 scalar contains both Ba bar Chiyya bar Ashi and Ba in the name of Chiyya bar Ashi. These supply the two formulas discussed by Hyman without proving an abbreviation’s corruption history. Hyman’s רח״בא is contextually Chiyya bar Abba and may be a general parallel for Abba’s reports, rather than a second name for Ashi. The earlier categorical heading/body-conflict description is therefore qualified; source pagination28b and the emendation remain distinct questions.

In the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 7:2:32, the Hebrew first reads “Rabbi Ba bar Chiya bar Ashi” and then “Rabbi Ba in the name of Rabbi Chiya bar Ashi.” The English edition’s note proposes reading the first as a report in Rabbi Chiya bar Ashi’s name, as in the next sentence. Hyman separately cites Rabbi Chiya bar Abba as a parallel for the reporting formula.
